C45023.observed: What was checked: where the edit row appears, and whether it offers the same boxes as the add row. What happened: clicking the edit control on the part "ZZAUTOTEST tv validation" opened a row immediately underneath that part's own line - the part line ends and the edit row begins about twenty pixels below it, with nothing in between - and the rest of the parts list simply moved down to make room. The row offers the same three boxes as the add row, in the same order: Description, Part number, Qty.

C45025.observed: What was checked: whether the edit row behaves like the add row, and whether its keyboard hint is worded for editing rather than adding. What happened: the boxes, the Tab order and the validation all behaved identically to the add row - Tab went Description, Part number, Qty, Save, Cancel and then back round to Description without leaving the row, there was no "More options" button, and clearing the description was refused with the same style of message. The hint line under the edit row reads "Enter save · Tab next field · Esc cancel" - it says just "save", without the add row's "& next row", which is right because saving a change does not open another row.
C45025.not_observed: The "Pulled from" bin chip Tab stop is covered by the Bin Allocation cases (Story 7) and was not exercised here.

C45026.observed: What was checked: whether saving a change updates the part where it sits, rather than adding another one. What happened: the quantity on "ZZAUTOTEST tv validation" was changed from 2 to 5 and saved. The row closed by itself and that same part line - in the same place in the list, with no extra line created - now reads 5. The list went back to its normal read-only display straight away.

C45034.observed: What was checked: whether the inline edit refuses to save on the grounds that someone else might have touched the part. What happened: the quantity was changed and saved and it simply went through - the row closed and the part line showed the new value. No "this part was changed by someone else" warning appeared and nothing was blocked, which matches how the product works today: it does not watch for two people editing the same part at once, so your save is never held up by that.

C45013.observed: What was checked: what happens to a part that is typed in by hand rather than picked from the catalogue. What happened: a description that matches nothing in the catalogue was typed in with a quantity and saved. The usual "Part added" confirmation appeared - the same one every save gives - and the part joined the list carrying the status "Requested", with a "(-)" where a part number would normally be and its row shaded in the same highlighted band as the other parts still waiting for their details. So the parts department can see at a glance which parts still need looking up.
